answer_text: Physical activity: at least 30 minutes of regular activity for at least 5 days a week (150 minutes a week). Salt: a maximum of 1 teaspoon (5 g) of salt for the whole day, including salt in cooking; avoid pickles, papad and packaged salty snacks. (NCD-3.1).

1st and 3rd trimester - No anaemia: 11.0 or more - Mild: 10.0–10.9 - Moderate: 7.0–9.9 - Severe: below 7.0 2nd trimester - No anaemia: 10.5 or more - Mild: 9.5–10.4 - Moderate: 7.0–9.4 - Severe: below 7.0 (ANC-3.1).

DANGER SIGN - REFER IMMEDIATELY (call 108/102). If the person is unconscious, having fits, or does not improve after the sugar, refer immediately (call 108). A diabetes patient with sweating, tremors, confusion, fast heartbeat, dizziness or blurred vision may have low sugar (below 70 mg/dl). (ESC-6.3).
If the child vomits, wait 10 minutes, then continue more slowly. Age: Up to 2 years - ORS after each loose stool: **50 to 100 ml** (CHD-1.2).
After delivery: one Red IFA tablet daily for 180 days (up to 6 months after delivery). One Red IFA tablet daily for 180 days, starting from the second trimester of pregnancy. (ANC-2.2).
DANGER SIGN - REFER IMMEDIATELY (call 108/102). Not able to drink or breastfeed. Convulsions (fits) now or during this illness. (ESC-5.1).

DANGER SIGN - REFER IMMEDIATELY (call 108/102). Severe headache, blurring of vision, or swelling of the face and hands / swelling all over the body, or reduced urine with high BP — signs of pre-eclampsia. BP 140/90 or more in a pregnant woman (ANC-4.1). (ESC-2.3).
This is outside my protocol book. Please ask the Medical Officer / ANM (SCP-1.2).
Take with meals, never on an empty stomach. Do not take calcium and IFA tablets together, because calcium reduces iron absorption. (ANC-2.3).

Result: No acute malnutrition - MUAC: **12.5 cm or more** - Colour on the tape: green Result: Severe acute malnutrition (SAM) - **below 11.5 cm**, or **oedema of both feet** at any MUAC - Colour on the tape: red (NUT-1.2).
This is outside my protocol book. Please ask the Medical Officer / ANM (SCP-1.2).
MR-1 (measles-rubella) at 9 completed months to 12 months; can be given till 5 years of age. PCV booster (PCV-B) at 9–12 months (if delayed, completed before 2 years of age — see IMM-2.2). (IMM-2.3).
Vaccine: fIPV - Minimum gap between doses: 8 weeks Vaccine: Penta, OPV, RVV - Minimum gap between doses: 4 weeks (IMM-2.6).

Oedema check: press gently on the top of both feet; if a dent (pit) remains in both feet, the child has bilateral pitting oedema. Screen all children 6–59 months with the MUAC tape (mid-upper arm circumference) and look for bilateral pitting oedema (oedema of both feet). (NUT-1.1).
Do not bathe a low birth weight baby until its weight is 2000 g; clean with a soft, warm, wet cloth instead. Do not bathe the baby for the first 48 hours. (HBNC-2.2).

gracedays: a vaccine, Td dose, MUAC check or NCD follow-up is overdue when today is more than 28 days after its due date (four weekly session cycles missed). Every "becomes overdue 28 days after its due date" in this document means this. (VIS-1.3).
Check-up: 1st - When: Within 12 weeks (as soon as pregnancy is suspected) Check-up: 4th - When: Between 36 weeks and term (ANC-1.2).
DANGER SIGN - REFER IMMEDIATELY (call 108/102). Fever every day for more than 7 days. Fever with any general danger sign (ESC-5.1) or a stiff neck. (ESC-5.4).

Under Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA), a check-up by a doctor/specialist is held at government health facilities on the 9th of every month, for women in the second or third trimester. Mobilise every pregnant woman in the second or third trimester to attend at least one PMSMA check-up. (ANC-1.3).

Penta and RVV can be given till one year of age. If the child received at least one PCV dose before the first birthday, the remaining PCV doses are completed as early as possible, at least 2 months apart, within the "before 2 years" complete-immunisation window. (IMM-2.2).

A random blood sugar by glucostrip of 140 mg/dl or more is a suspected diabetes case → refer to the Medical Officer for confirmation. Diagnosis is made by the MO: fasting 126 mg/dl or more, or 2-hour post-meal 200 mg/dl or more, or HbA1c 6.5% or more, or random 200 mg/dl or more with symptoms of diabetes. (NCD-1.3).
This is outside my protocol book. Please ask the Medical Officer / ANM (SCP-1.2).
Vaccine: BCG - When: At birth or as early as possible - Upper limit: till one year of age Vaccine: Hepatitis B birth dose (HepB-0) - When: At birth - Upper limit: within 24 hours of birth (IMM-2.1).
Vitamin A 2nd dose (2 lakh IU, 2 ml) at 16–18 months, then one dose every 6 months up to 5 years of age (9 doses in all). Give the OPV/DPT booster at least 6 months after OPV-3/Penta-3. (IMM-2.4).
Dose: Td-2 - When: 4 weeks after Td-1 Dose: Td-Booster - When: If she received 2 TT/Td doses in a pregnancy within the last 3 years — then give only one booster dose (IMM-4.1).
Chandrapuri is not a JE-endemic district, so JE vaccine is not given here. MR-2, DPT booster-1 (DPT-B1), OPV booster (OPV-B); JE-2 only in endemic districts. (IMM-2.4).
This is outside my protocol book. Please ask the Medical Officer / ANM (SCP-1.2).

At each visit ask about bleeding (how many pads changed in a day), fever, foul-smelling discharge, pain, breast problems, fits or abnormal talk. Continue one Red IFA tablet daily for 180 days after delivery and calcium (two tablets a day) up to 6 months after delivery (ANC-2.2, ANC-2.3). (HBNC-3.1).

DANGER SIGN - REFER IMMEDIATELY (call 108/102). Convulsions (fits) now or during this illness. Lethargic or unconscious. (ESC-5.1).

After a caesarean delivery, visits start from day 7 (because mother and baby stay longer in hospital). Place of delivery: Institutional delivery - Number of home visits: 6 visits - Visit days: Days 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 and 42 (HBNC-1.1).

Place of delivery: Institutional delivery - Number of home visits: 6 visits - Visit days: Days 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 and 42 Place of delivery: Home delivery - Number of home visits: 7 visits - Visit days: Days 1, 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 and 42 (HBNC-1.1).
DANGER SIGN - REFER IMMEDIATELY (call 108/102). Weight less than 1.8 kg (refer to SNCU). Distended abdomen, or the baby vomits often. (ESC-4.4).
DANGER SIGN - REFER IMMEDIATELY (call 108/102). Continuous severe abdominal pain, or excessive vomiting — unable to take anything by mouth. (ESC-2.6).

Age: 2 months up to 12 months - Fast breathing: **50 breaths per minute or more** A child with cough or difficult breathing and fast breathing, or with chest indrawing or stridor (a harsh noise when breathing in) when calm, must be referred (ESC-5.2; for babies under 2 months ESC-4.2). (CHD-3.1).

Under Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK), pregnant women delivering in government facilities get free: delivery (including caesarean section), drugs, diagnostics, diet and blood; free transport from home to the health institution, between facilities in case of referral, and drop back home after 48 hours of stay. (ANC-5.3).
DANGER SIGN - REFER IMMEDIATELY (call 108/102). Hb below 7 g/dL (severe anaemia), or severe pallor with or without breathlessness. Fast or difficult breathing, or breathlessness at rest. (ESC-2.5).
DANGER SIGN - REFER IMMEDIATELY (call 108/102). Heavy bleeding: a pad is soaked in less than 5 minutes, or more than 5 pads are changed in a day. (ESC-3.1).

DANGER SIGN - REFER IMMEDIATELY (call 108/102). Baby is cold to touch, or temperature below 95.9 °F (35.5 °C). The newborn fever cut-off (more than 99 °F, from the HBNC home-visit form) is deliberately lower than the 37.5 °C used for older children in CHD-2.1. (ESC-4.3).
